newsitem.title: UK: From the Flightdeck - The air Cargo Week In Review.
newsitem.headline: From the Flightdeck - The air Cargo Week In Review.

text.p: This is Reuters' lookback at the major developments in the air cargo industry in the week October 18-25.
**OCTOBER 18**
FRANKFURT - Lufthansa Cargo launches global cargo partnership with UAL including joint rates, common sales and marketing.

MIAMI - Cargo carriers serving Latin America begin to slap fuel surcharges on some routes just as the busy season begins - SINGAPORE - Industry sources says Asian retail air fares are likely to rise before the end of the year due to sustained high jet fuel costs.

MOSCOW - Freight forwarders say rates for cargo operations from Moscow's Sheremetyevo international airport have fallen over the last four weeks as the market becomes more active- PARIS - Nice Cote d'Azur airport reports a 7.9 percent increase in airfreight traffic in September from year ago on volume of 1,517 tonnes.
PARIS - Brest's Guipavas airport handled 2,391 tonnes of global cargo traffic in Jan-sept, up 22.4 percent on year ago.
FORT WORTH - American Airlines U.S. cargo sales VP says it has seen especially early start to the pre-Christmas air freight peak.
DENVER - Frontier Airlines agrees to lease a new Boeing 737-300 jet from GE Capital Aviation Services.
WASHINGTON - Federal aviation officials say the biggest drag on aviation growth in the U.S. is the shortage of airport capacity with no new airports to be built soon.
PARIS - Air France chairman expects an alliance with an Asian carrier in 1997 after recent pacts with Delta Air Lines and Continental.
JOHANNESBURG - SAA lodges formal complaint with licensing authorities over a franchise agreement between BA and local carrier Comair.
DUBAI - TIACA president Ram Menen concerned over new U.S. FAA security rules for air cargo, which he says were issued without any input or involvement from the industry.
* Menen says Internet offers an opportunity to fast forward the air cargo industry into the new communications era and those who do not seize the initiative will become as extinct as dinosaurs.
* Menen says trading could one day be possible in air cargo rate futures.
** OCTOBER 21**
SEOUL - Korean Air agrees to supply $600 million worth of aircraft parts to Boeing until 2006.
BEIJING - The Xinhua Daily Telegraph says China has completed constructions of an airport near the huge Three Gorges dam project on the Yangtze river.
DUBAI - Lufthansa and Singapore Airlines to interchange cargoes at Sharjah in a bid to cut operating costs from next week in winter schedules.
MAASTRICHT - The Netherlands' most southerly airport has bowed to public pressure and will ban all flights of IIyushin 76 aircraft from November 15.
WARSAW - Poland's national carrier LOT will increase the number of flights in the winter season starting October 29.
MOSCOW - Vnukovo Airlines will add two new Tupolev-204 passenger and cargo jets to fleet this week.
COPENHAGEN - SAS to form an alliance with SAA to gain foothold on the African continent.
PARIS - Airfreight handled at Pau-Pyrenees airport totalled 903.9 tonnes in Jan-Sep, down 1.9 percent on year ago.
ZURICH - Swissair shares fell below 1,000 Swiss francs and stayed under pressure on worries about higher fuel prices, fare wars and its partner Delta's link-up with Air France.
COPENHAGEN - SAS plans to open regional freight depot on western Denmark's Jutland peninsula next year.
DUBAI - Schenker International vice-president Klaus Geissler says freight forwarders "will fight" to maintain their right to deal with exporters and distributors at a retail level.
PARIS - Nantes-Atlantique airport air cargo traffic in Jan-Aug totalled 1,561 tonnes up 11.3 percent on the same period in 1995.
COPENHAGEN - Danish news agency Rizhau says ground staff at SAS are threatening to strike this week and next, but airline management is unperturbed.
HONG KONG - BA to employ a fourth weekly freighter on HK-Lon route next year.
*BA Asian cargo manager Chris Humphrey confident of a "dramatic improvement" in freight handling service standards at London's Gatwick and Heathrow airports.
DUBAI - Emirates says it has taken delivery if its third Boeing 777 aircraft.
HONG KONG - Cathay Pacific successfully handled its first load of pigs destined for breeding in China.
ARLINGTON - USAir says that its total traffic was up 6.3 percent in the third quarter on a capacity hike of 1.3 percent.
LONDON - United Airlines says it flew 206 million cargo tonne miles during September or 7.7 percent more than a year ago.
DUBAI - U.S. dept of transportation deputy director of negotiations Susan McDermott says the U.S. and Britain have "not yet found common ground" in talks on opening their aviation markets.
*McDermott says governments should open their aviation industries to international carriers and let market forces dictate.
BRUSSELS - Antwerp port authority begins work on a six billion Belgian franc, multi-berth dock at port with a capacity to handle up to nine million tonnes of cargo a year.

DUBAI - Singapore Airlines cargo chief Huang Cheng Eng says passengers and combined passenger/cargo airlines should boost demand to overcome present excess airfreight capacity in order to deal with "plunging yields."
LONDON - BA and the privately-owned British Mediterranean Airways will not be proceeding with their proposed franchise agreement because BMA had not met all conditions.
FRANKFURT - Airport authority says cargo capacity on freighter flights leaving Frankfurt will rise five percent this winter.
-Seven airlines will launch new services from Frankfurt this winter.
-Germany air cargo market continues its recovery of the last few months.
-Frankfurt passenger numbers fell 0.4 percent in Sept.

BRUSSELS - EU Commission spokeswoman says "Not bad but could do better" appears to be the conclusion of EC report on airlines' response to the EU's gradual liberalisation of the civil aviation market.
BRUSSELS - Sabena says Swissair subsidiary Crossair will fly Brussels-Berne six times a week this winter in a code-sharing agreement with Sabena.
SAN FRANCISCO - An airport spokesman says the FAA has authorised San Francisco International airport to contribute about $197 million to a $1.2 billion rail extension project.
LONDON - BA world cargo appoints Geoff Corpe to the newly-created role of general manager worldwide sales and marketing.
LONDON - Heavylift-VolgaDnepr adds ninth Antonov 124-100 to its fleet.
CHICAGO - TWA says that it and Boeing were named in a suit filed in New York alleging mechanical malfunction and negligence in connection with the July 17 crash off Long Island.
**OCTOBER 22**
KABUL - Official radio Afghanistan says state-owned Ariana Airlines will open flights between Kabul and the Pakistan capital of Islamabad.
SEOUL - The president of aero-engine joint venture GE-P&W Engine Alliance Larry Scott close to a memorandum of understanding with Airbus Industrie consortium to supply superjumbo engines.
HANOI - Vietnam's Pacific Airlines official says it will start a twice-a-week service to Macau from Ho Chi Minh City next month.
BANGKOK - Finance minister says Thai cabinet approved in principal a finance ministry proposal to sell an undisclosed percent of its shares in Thai Airways International.
